title: Generation, High-Throughput Screening, and Biobanking of Human-Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Cardiac Spheroids
protocol: Equilibrate penicillin-streptomycin and RPMI 1640 medium to room temperature (RT) and ensure they have thawed completely.
Mix 500 mL of the medium with 5 mL of pen/strep.
Store the mixed medium at 4 °C for up to 8 weeks; equilibrate to 37 °C before use.
Equilibrate B27 supplement and basal medium to RT.
Ensure the B27 supplement has thawed completely.
Mix 490 mL of basal medium with 10 mL of 50x B27 supplement.
Store the RPMI + B27 at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks; equilibrate to 37 °C before use.
Add Rho-associated, coiled-coil containing protein kinase (ROCK) inhibitor at a final concentration of 2 µM and 10% knockout serum replacement (KSR) to RPMI + B27 media for re-plating hiPSC-CMs.
Do not store culture media once supplemented with ROCK inhibitor.
Add a 1:100 concentration of cell survival supplement and 20% KSR to RPMI + B27 media for thawing hiPSC-CMs.
Equilibrate the CM thawing media to 37 °C before use.
Remove 65 mL from a bottle of DMEM without glucose.

Supplement the removed DMEM with 2.7 g of glucose, 5.6 g of L-lactate, 0.025 mg of vitamin B12, 1 mg of biotin, 3.73 g of creatine monohydrate, 1.25 g of taurine, 1.975 g of L-carnitine, 0.7125 g of ascorbic acid, and 50 mL of NEAA.
Add 12.5 g of albumax to the supplemented DMEM.
Mix in 5 mL of penicillin-streptomycin.
Filter the mixture through a sterile disposable filter unit with a 0.22 μm pore Polyethersulfone membrane.
Aliquot into 45 mL or 4.5 mL portions based on required volume.
Store aliquots at -20°C for up to 6 months.
Equilibrate B27 supplement, knockout SR, penicillin-streptomycin, and maturation supplement at room temperature.
Thaw the maturation supplement completely.
Mix 435 mL of DMEM no glucose medium with 10 mL of 50x B27 supplement, 5 mL of penicillin-streptomycin, 5 mL of knockout SR, and 45 mL of maturation supplement.
Store the mixture at 4°C for up to 2 weeks; equilibrate at 37°C before use.
Equilibrate penicillin-streptomycin at room temperature (RT).
Ensure penicillin-streptomycin is completely thawed.
Mix 500 mL of DMEM fluorobrite medium with 5 mL of penicillin-streptomycin.
Store the mixture at 4 °C for up to 1 month; equilibrate at 37 °C before use.
Mix 20% w/v non-ionic detergent powder (e.g., F-127) with PBS.
Filter the mixture using a 0.22 µm filter and store at 4 °C for up to 6 months; equilibrate at RT before use.
Mix the non-ionic detergent solution (final concentration of 0.04% v/v) with 0.1x calcium dye (e.g., Cal520 AM) in fluor bright medium.
In a 50 mL conical tube, add 10 µL of Cal520 and 20 µL of the non-ionic detergent solution.
Mix until fully dissolved.
Keep the solution in the dark before adding to cells.
Prepare permeabilization and blocking buffer containing 10 mL PBS, 5% wt/v BSA, and 0.3% v/v Triton-X-100.
Prepare flow cytometry buffer containing 50 mL PBS, 1% wt/v BSA, and 0.3% v/v Triton-X-100.
Prepare flow cytometry washing buffer containing 50 mL PBS and 1% wt/v BSA.
Prepare spheroid washing buffer (SWB) containing 1 mL Triton-X-100, 2 mL of 10% w/v SDS in DPBS, and 2 g BSA in 1 L PBS.
Store SWB at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.
Prepare the embedding solution by mixing 50 mL of glycerol, 9.09 mL of dH2O, 1 mL of Tris buffer (1 M, pH 8.0), and 200 µL of EDTA (0.5 M).
Add 22.7 g of fructose to the mixture and mix at room temperature in the dark until dissolved.
When clear, add an additional 22.2 g of fructose to the solution and mix until dissolved.
Then add 15 g of urea and mix until completely dissolved; store at 4 °C in the dark.
Prepare PBT buffer by mixing PBS with Tween-20 (0.1% v/v).
For 1 L of PBS, add 1 mL of Tween-20 to create the PBT buffer solution.
Reconstitute thiazovivin powder in 50 µL aliquots of 10 mM DMSO and store at -20 °C for up to 6 months; protect from light.
Prepare Cal-520 AM in 10 µL aliquots of 2.5 mM DMSO and store them at -20 °C for up to 6 months; protect from light.
Seed up to 1 million CMs in a 6-well ultra-low attachment plate with 2 mL of hiPSC-CM re-plating media when generating cardiac spheroids.
When cultured hiPSC-CMs reach confluence, add 0.1 mL/cm² of sterile cardiac detachment solution (e.g., trypsin) to each well.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C for 15 min.
Using a 5 mL pipet, mechanically dissociate the cells by flushing with 2 mL of warm basal medium to make a single cell suspension.
Confirm the detachment with a bright field microscope (4x magnification); cells will look white and have a round shape.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube and centrifuge for 3 min at 300 x g.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 1 mL of hiPSC-CM re-plating media.
Mechanically dissociate the cell pellet using a 1,000 µL pipet tip.
The solution appears homogeneous after three or four mixes.
Count the cells.
Transfer the appropriate amount of cells in 100 µL of the re-plating medium to each ultra-low attachment round-bottom 96-well well.
Place the plate of CSs on an orbital shaker at 70 rpm in the incubator for 24 h.
Set the incubator conditions to 37 °C, 5% CO2, 21% O2, and 90% humidity.
Aspirate 50 µL of medium from each well and add 100 µL of RPMI + B27 medium per well for the first 48 h.
Maintain 50 µL of the medium in the 96-well plate to avoid accidental aspiration and spheroid rupture.
Aspirate 100 µL of the medium from each well and add 100 µL of the maturation medium per well.
Maintain the cells in the maturation medium and refresh the medium every 2-3 days.
Pre-cool the plate by placing it on ice for 10 min.
Centrifuge the spheroid plate for 3 min at 70 x g.
Remove the supernatant until 50 μL remains and add 200 μL of ice-cold hiPSC freezing medium per well.
Keep the CS suspension on ice for the entire duration of the procedure.
Freeze one well in a 500 μL freezing medium cryovial if using a 6-well plate with spheroids.
Seal the plate with plate sealing film.
Store the 96-well plate in a polystyrene box or a silicon mold for uniform heat exchange during freezing.
Mix two components of the silicon elastomer kit in a 10:1 ratio vigorously.
De-bubble the solution using a vacuum pump for 15-20 min.
Cast the de-bubbled solution inside the bottom part of the well plate and continue to de-bubble using a vacuum pump for 10 min.
Place the mold into an oven and cure at 60 °C for 8 h to obtain a semi-flexible elastomer that is peeled off the plate.
Freeze the plate at -80 °C for a minimum of 4 h in the polystyrene box or the prepared silicon mold.
Transfer the plate to a liquid nitrogen tank or a -150 °C freezer for long-term storage.
Prepare 20 mL of 37 °C preheated basal medium in a 50 mL conical tube.
Collect the cell plate with CSs from the liquid nitrogen and place it in the incubator for 15 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend each well in warm basal medium using 200 µL of medium per well.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 70 x g.
Repeat steps to remove the supernatant until the cell pellet remains, then add 200 µL of CM thawing medium in each well.
Place the plate of CSs on an orbital shaker at 70 rpm in an incubator for 24 h.
Aspirate 50 µL of the medium from each well and add 100 µL of RPMI + B27 medium per well for the first 48 h.
Aspirate 100 µL of the medium from each well and add 100 µL of maturation medium per well.
Maintain the cells in the maturation media and refresh the medium every 2-3 days.
After 1 week of culture, treat thawed CSs with 100 μL of calcium dye medium per well.
Incubate the treated cells for 60 min in an incubator set to 37 °C, 5% CO2, 21% O2, and 90% humidity.
Power the microscope, ensuring the environmental control option is on.
Adjust the camera and framing aperture dimensions to minimize background area.
Record a video with a consistent stream of 2−10 peaks within 10 s across a 96-well plate in a zig-zag pattern.
Measure the calcium signal using a 488 nm laser; set the contrast to a black background with a bright green signal during calcium release.
Analyze the data with fluorescence traces analysis software according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Collect cardiac spheroids in a 15 mL conical tube using a 5 mL pipette to avoid damage.
Centrifuge the collected cardiac spheroids for 3 minutes at 70 x g.
Aspirate the supernatant and add 1 mL of PBS.
Centrifuge again for 3 minutes at 200 x g.
Aspirate the supernatant and add 1 mL of cardiac detachment solution (e.g., trypLE).
Incubate at 37 °C for 15 minutes.
Mechanically dissociate cells using a 5 mL pipette, flushing with basal medium until single cells are visible under a microscope.
Centrifuge the dissociated cells for 3 minutes at 200 x g.
Aspirate the supernatant and fix the cardiac myocytes (CMs) with 200 µL of 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS.
Incubate fixed CMs for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge the fixed cells for 3 minutes at 200 x g.
Aspirate the supernatant and add 1 mL of PBS.
Transfer cell suspension to a FACS tube and centrifuge for 3 minutes at 200 x g.
Resuspend 1 x 10^5 cells in 50 µL of permeabilization buffer.
Incubate the cells for 30 minutes at 4 °C.
Resuspend the cells in flow cytometry buffer containing α-actinin antibody at a dilution of 1:300.
Resuspend 1 x 10^5 cells in flow cytometry buffer with FITC mouse IgM, κ isotype control at a dilution of 1:200.
Resuspend 1 x 10^5 cells in flow cytometry buffer for negative control.
Incubate the cells for 30 min at 4 °C.
Add 2.5 mL of flow cytometry buffer and centrifuge the cells at 200 x g for 3 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and repeat the washing step twice.
Resuspend the cells in flow cytometry buffer with secondary-antibody goat-anti-mouse at a dilution of 1:300.
Place the tube in the dark since the secondary-antibody solution is light-sensitive.
Add 150 µL of propidium iodide (PI) per sample at a dilution of 1:1,000 and incubate for 15 min.
Place the tube in the dark since the PI solution is light-sensitive.
Adjust the gates according to the standard gating strategy.
Analyze the cells with a flow cytometer.
Coat pipet tips and conical tubes with 1% wt/v BSA-PBS to prevent spheroids from sticking to plastics.
Collect cardiac spheroids in a 15 mL coated tube using a 5 mL pipet.
Centrifuge the collected spheroids for 3 min at 70 x g.
Aspirate the supernatant and carefully resuspend the spheroids in 1 mL of ice-cold 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) solution in 1x PBS using a coated 1 mL tip.
Fix the spheroids at 4 °C for 45 min, gently resuspending them after 20 min.
Add 10 mL of ice-cold PBS to the tube and mix by inverting.
Incubate for 10 min at 4 °C and spin down at 70 x g for 3 min.
Resuspend the pellet in ice-cold SWB (200 µL of SWB per well) and transfer the spheroids to a 24-well suspension culture plate.
Split CSs from one large pellet over multiple wells for different stainings.
Incubate CSs at 4°C for at least 15 min.
Add 200 µL of SWB in an empty well as a reference well.
Allow spheroids to settle at the bottom of the plate by tilting it at a 45° angle for 5 min.
Remove SWB, leaving CSs in 200 µL of SWB.
Add 200 µL of SWB with primary antibodies (e.g., α-actinin [1:200] and Troponin T [1:200]) at 2x concentration and incubate overnight at 4°C while rocking/shaking (40 rpm on a horizontal shaker).
Add 1 mL of SWB to each well the next day.
Allow CSs to settle at the bottom of the plate by tilting it at a 45° angle for 5 min.
Remove SWB, leaving 200 µL in each well.
Add 1 mL of SWB and wash for 2 h with slow rocking/shaking.
Repeat steps including adding 1 mL of SWB and washing twice more.
Allow CSs to settle at the bottom of the plate by tilting it at a 45° angle for 5 min.
Remove SWB, leaving 200 µL in each well.
Add 200 µL of the secondary antibodies, conjugated antibodies, and dyes 2x concentrated to the sample.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C in the dark while rocking/shaking slowly.
Repeat steps of incubation twice more the next day.
Transfer CSs to a 1.5 mL tube and spin down at 70 x g for 3 min.
Remove as much supernatant as possible without disrupting the CSs by pipetting.
Add at least 50 µL of embedding solution (ES) using a modified 200 µL tip.
Resuspend CSs gently in ES to prevent bubble formation and incubate at RT for 20 min.
Create a square container on a glass slide with nail polish or silicone sealant.
Transfer the CSs in ES to the middle of the square container.
Place a square coverslip on top, reducing air bubbles by lowering it from one side.
Gently push on all edges of the coverslip to seal it to the nail polish or silicone sealant.
Leave the slide overnight at RT for imaging.
